scope: Initial core diff review plus a narrow static follow-up of the dissolve endpoint/lifecycle fix in VIDEO_StepPortraitTransition, VIDEO_EndPortraitTransition, caller ordering, ending.c cleanup, and the added endpoint unit test. No builds, tests, resource renders, game/UI, repository/Git/Issue/configuration mutations, or network writes were performed by this reviewer.
conclusion: R3-C1 is resolved in the reviewed source snapshot. No remaining blocker identified in this narrow endpoint/lifecycle follow-up; this is static review, not real-game acceptance.

findings.title: The 12th dissolve step exposes an unfinished native index at old-portrait-only pixels
findings.cause: VIDEO_StepPortraitTransition restores the source coverage immediately when step>=steps. At old-portrait-only pixels the source has no coverage, so the just-displayed frame falls back to the target native index. The native 12-round dissolve advances its low nibble only11 times because round0 does not advance it, whereas its full possible distance is15.
findings.concrete_example: At a pixel covered by the old portrait only, backup index0 and source index15 result in native index11 in round12; the reverse yields4. Earlier portrait-region frames follow RGB interpolation toward the actual source pixel, but the final transition frame unexpectedly switches to palette[11]/palette[4], then the final VIDEO_UpdateScreen/source copy displays the true target.
findings.not_generalized: The16-round FBP path has enough low-nibble steps to reach distance15; wipe copies native indices exactly. These do not establish that the12-round case is safe.
findings.minimal_fix: Display exact composed after RGB for the final transition step; return the target plane to source tags/coverage only after the final transition frame has been shown (for example in EndPortraitTransition). Preserve all native index writes.
findings.recommended_check: Use an old-portrait-only pixel with index0->15 and15->0. At the12th displayed step assert exact after RGB while native index remains11/4, then assert End/final-frame source coverage. The existing same-background-index7 test does not exercise this.
findings.validation: Static control/data-flow and explicit nibble arithmetic; no test or game execution.

resolution.video.c:369-390: Step always writes tagged literal RGB. At step==steps each component equals after RGB exactly; it no longer releases the old-only mask to an unfinished native nibble.
resolution.video.c:395-410: End restores source tags/coverage only in the original transition mask union, then frees the snapshots/mask. Source without a companion layer yields zero coverage.
resolution.video.c:1386-1426: Switch displays each phase before End, then copies the source to backup and updates the final source screen.
resolution.video.c:1575-1595: Fade displays the last transition phase before End, then displays the intact source frame. Its native nibble formula is unchanged.
resolution.battle.c:274-294: Battle copies and displays the last RGB phase before End; the final full source copy removes temporary literal tags from gpScreen.
resolution.ending.c:127-155: FBP displays all16 phases, then End normalizes backup coverage and VIDEO_ClearPortraits(gpScreen) clears literal tags previously copied into gpScreen. This also runs for the special last FBP branch that skips the ordinary full FBP repaint.

test_review.reviewed_assertions: Both0->15 and15->0 directions preserve native low nibbles11/4 while asserting the last composed portrait-region RGB is exactly the target color. Then it checks the final copied source frame.
test_review.boundary: The test was read, not executed by this reviewer. The final copy can itself normalize coverage, so the separate End tag restoration is confirmed here by static code/caller-order inspection, not attributed to a standalone End-state test assertion.

accepted_static_properties: SDL1 retains VIDEO_PortraitLayer=NULL and no companion allocation. When both source/target lack companion planes, Begin returnsNULL; Step/End are no-ops.
Portrait source index tags remain distinct from transparent0 and opaque black; transition literal RGB uses a separate0xFF tag.
Wave shifts the companion row by the same positive wraparound offset as the existing320-pixel index row. The320 shift is correctly a no-op for both.
Normal transitions visit all six native byte phases; RGB interpolation is restricted to the original source/target coverage union.
Caller-owned PAL_ReadPalette is retained in composition/current-color lookup; the reviewed changes do not reintroduce the earlier shared PAL_GetPalette buffer overwrite.
Palette effect additions update a separate portrait color table while existing scene palette formulas and native index writes remain intact.
PAL_MakeScene/PAL_FBPBlitToSurface and normal coverage-invalidating drawing keep their existing layer-clearing/occlusion roles; no new default resource/config change is introduced by this diff.
boundaries: This reviewer performed source inspection only; no build, unit test, rendering, real game, emulator, OS window, or hardware-equivalence verification was run.
The no-blocker follow-up conclusion applies to the reviewed endpoint/lifecycle change and listed file hashes, not an unreviewed later diff or the whole engine.
Original Saturn evidence remains in source-review.json. The implementation is explicitly a PC-compatible effect policy, not a proven frame-for-frame Saturn replica.
Real-game acceptance remains for the user; the main agent reported source-render verification does not substitute for it.
followup_static_acceptance: At the last RGB interpolation step, integer arithmetic computes b*steps/steps with a coefficient of zero, eliminating the premature native-index fallback.

All reviewed normal callers call End only after the final transition display; subsequent normal copies or the explicit FBP gpScreen cleanup prevent transition RGB tags from surviving into the next palette effect.
FBP cleanup preserves native pixels and any already-drawn ordinary effect sprite; it clears only the companion plane, so the special no-repaint ending branch does not retain stale literal RGB.
No new repository changes were made by this reviewer.
